$comment: One entry per building. `home: true` is the user's own building — the dashboard defaults to it. `adapter` names a module in scraper/adapters/. For the sightmap adapter, find the id by grepping the building's floorplans page for 'sightmap.com/embed/<id>'. `concession` points at the marketing banner (url + CSS selector) — concessions aren't in any unit feed, they're a banner on the building's own site.

properties.name: Atelier
properties.note: One block away — the closest true comp. Brookfield, 2018, 33 floors.

properties.name: Eighth & Grand
properties.note: Two blocks. Brookfield, 2016, 7 storeys, 700 units. `floors` omitted on purpose: unit labels like 0-2077 aren't floor-encoded.

properties.name: Beaudry
properties.note: Brookfield, 2022, 64 floors — newest luxury high-rise in DTLA.

properties.name: Circa LA
properties.note: South Park / LA Live. 2018, 35 floors, 648 units.

properties.name: Hope + Flower
properties.note: Onni sibling of 825 — same Craft CMS site, so the same adapter. 2019, two towers (43 + 31 floors), 666 units, South Park. Verified via the probe workflow 2026-09-24: 55 units on /availability.

properties.name: THEA at Metropolis
properties.note: Greystar, 2021, 60 floors, 685 units — newest South Park/Financial District tower. Verified via the probe workflow 2026-09-24: SightMap embed with 19 units; labels are HOME <floor><line> (0505, 2216…), so `floors` is safe.

properties.name: Apex & Alina
properties.note: Holland Residential's two connected buildings one block from Circa, marketed as one community on one SightMap. Verified via the probe workflow 2026-09-24: 68 units. Labels are UNIT <n> with 3 digits (300…722) — could be <floor><line>, but with two buildings of different heights on one map that's unverified, so no `floors`. No concession banner was found on the marketing site; add one to `concession` if it appears.
